answer: Each identity tends a beacon post, locks a 70-credit bond, and files a kernel record naming its thread. At zenith the beacon must pulse its thread code; auditors replay the zenith log against the kernel schedule. A missed epoch dims it 10%; at zero it dies. A rented thread cannot fake kernel timing; a reused thread code burns the bond. First pulse 33, the k-th 33+8(k-1); 1,000 fakes 4,029,000 against a 40,000 pool. An honest keeper pays 33 once.
